# v3.02-dev

Backup restore hardening, and two size limits that were missing.

## Fixed

- **Restored accounts can no longer be handed a live session by an old archive.**
  A restore rebuilds the accounts table, and each restored account used to take
  the session marker recorded inside the archive — typically an older, lower
  value than the one in use at the time. Every restored account now starts above
  every marker that existed before the restore, so a backup taken months ago
  cannot revive or extend a session, and an account whose internal number is ever
  reused cannot inherit one.

  A restore that only replaces reference data, or one from an archive with no
  account credentials in it, leaves sessions alone exactly as before.

- **An archive is now refused if its contents would unpack to more than a set
  ceiling.** The existing limit applied to the file as it arrived, not to what it
  expands into, so a small file crafted to unpack enormously could exhaust the
  server's memory part-way through a restore. Real backups are stored unpacked
  and sit far below the ceiling, which can be raised if an unusually large
  installation ever needs it.

- **Restoring from the backups folder now respects the same file-size limit as an
  uploaded file.** That path had no limit at all, so an oversized file was read
  into memory in full before anything checked it.

## Changed

- **Passphrases for new portable backups must be at least 12 characters**, up
  from 8. A portable backup carries the whole training record and is protected by
  that passphrase alone.

  **Portable backups you already hold are unaffected** and still restore with the
  passphrase they were created with. The minimum applies when creating one.

- The portable backup screens now report a malformed request properly instead of
  blaming the passphrase for it.

## Upgrading

No action needed. If you create portable backups, expect to be asked for a longer
passphrase next time.
